name: rice-ranking-with-override
description: Test that RICE ranking uses absolute reach, one effort unit and defensible confidence, that the script is actually run, and that a strategic override is recorded with a reason rather than silently reordering the list.
test_input: features.json has 7 candidate features for 2026-Q1 with reach as account counts per quarter, impact on the canonical 3/2/1/0.5/0.25 scale, confidence as a decimal, and effort in engineer-weeks. Two of them are 'SSO/SAML' (reach 90, impact 3, confidence 0.9, effort 12) and 'Bulk CSV import' (reach 1400, impact 2, confidence 0.8, effort 6). Run scripts/rice_scorer.py and tell me what to build first.
expected_output: A ranked markdown table from the script with reach, impact, confidence, effort and score visible per row, Bulk CSV import ranked above SSO/SAML on score, and an explicit statement that SSO is worth keeping despite a lower score because enterprise deals require it — recorded as an override with its reason, not as a re-scored item.
assertions: scripts/rice_scorer.py is executed rather than the scores being estimated by hand
Every row shows all four inputs, not just the final score
Reach is reported as an absolute count (accounts per quarter), never a 1-5 rating
Bulk CSV import outranks SSO/SAML on RICE score
The SSO recommendation is preserved via a labeled override that names strategy or dependency as the reason
The output states that RICE ranks but does not decide

name: interview-synthesis-evidence-discipline
description: Test that raw interview notes become behavior-named themes with participant counts, verbatim evidence and a counter-evidence section — not a narrative summary of the most quotable users.
test_input: Here are 14 customer interview transcripts from a B2B analytics tool (mixed enterprise and mid-market, 2 churned users). Synthesize what we learned and tell me what to build.
expected_output: A TL;DR of three sentences, then themes ranked by participants x severity where each theme is named by the behavior (e.g. 'rebuilds the weekly export in Excel every Monday'), carries a distinct-participant count of at least 3, names the segments present, quotes verbatim evidence with participant IDs, and states the current workaround. Followed by signals below the 3-participant threshold, a counter-evidence section, and open questions. No feature recommendations until the themes are established.
assertions: Output opens with a three-sentence TL;DR before any theme detail
Each theme names a behavior rather than a topic noun
Each theme reports a count of distinct participants and the segments represented
Themes below the 3-participant threshold are listed separately as signals, not promoted to themes
Verbatim quotes are attributed to participant IDs
A counter-evidence section exists and contains at least one item
Current workaround is stated per theme
The two churned users are distinguishable in the segment breakdown

name: prd-scope-and-kill-criteria
description: Test that a PRD request produces a bounded scope contract with must/should/won't split, one primary metric with baseline and window, and kill criteria — and that a vagueness in the brief is surfaced as an open question rather than invented away.
test_input: Write a PRD for 'make onboarding faster' for our project-management SaaS. We have 3,400 teams, activation (first shared project within 7 days) is 34%, and the exec wants it shipped this quarter.
expected_output: A 2-4 page PRD with a problem statement citing the 34% baseline, a one-sentence vision, at most two personas, a must/should/won't-have split where the won't-have list is named explicitly, requirements written as testable acceptance criteria, one primary metric (activation 34% -> a stated target by a stated date) plus guardrails, kill criteria written before launch, and an open-questions list that flags 'faster' and the exec's quarter deadline as decisions needing an owner.
assertions: A 'Won't have this time' list is present and names at least one adjacent thing stakeholders would assume is included
Requirements are testable and follow an as-a/I-can/so-that plus acceptance form
Exactly one primary metric is named, with the 34% baseline, a target and a measurement window
Kill criteria are stated before any launch or rollout plan
At most two personas are defined
Open questions carry an owner and a decide-by date
The ambiguous term 'faster' is flagged rather than silently interpreted

name: okr-output-versus-outcome
description: Test that a draft OKR set containing output-style key results is diagnosed and rewritten into leading/lagging outcome KRs with baselines, and that confidence is rated at the start of the quarter.
test_input: Here are our draft Q1 OKRs for the platform team: Objective 'Be the most reliable platform in the category.' KRs: (1) Ship the new deployment pipeline by March 15, (2) Launch the status page redesign, (3) Complete the observability migration. Fix these.
expected_output: A diagnosis that all three KRs are outputs/tasks with no baseline, then a rewritten set of 2-4 outcome KRs each with baseline, target and date, at least one lagging KR (e.g. p95 incident recovery time, error budget burn) and one or more leading KRs, a high/medium/low confidence rating per KR with the assumption that would break it, and a note on how the shipped work becomes an input rather than a key result.
assertions: All three original KRs are identified as output/task statements
Every rewritten KR has a numeric baseline and a target with a date
At least one lagging KR is present and labeled as lagging
At least one leading KR is present and labeled as leading
Each KR carries a high/medium/low confidence rating made at the start of the quarter
The output states that shipping the pipeline is an input to a KR, not a KR itself
Scoring guidance (0-1 scale, ~0.7 is a good stretch quarter) is stated

name: negative-launch-plan-out-of-scope
description: Test that a launch/channel request is routed to go-to-market-launch rather than answered with PM toolkit content.
test_input: Plan our Product Hunt launch for next Tuesday — tagline, gallery frames, first comment, and the day-of schedule.
expected_output: A short routing response identifying this as a go-to-market / launch-execution task and pointing to the go-to-market-launch skill, without producing a PH runbook from this skill.
assertions: The response identifies the request as out of scope for product-manager-toolkit
go-to-market-launch is named as the correct skill
No Product Hunt runbook, tagline or gallery plan is produced
The boundary is stated in terms of what this skill does cover (prioritization, PRDs, OKRs, synthesis)

name: negative-pricing-decision-out-of-scope
description: Test that a price/packaging question is not answered with product management frameworks, and that the skill does not invent a price.
test_input: We're launching a Pro tier. What should it cost, and which features go in it versus the free plan?
expected_output: A routing response identifying pricing and packaging as out of scope and naming pricing-strategist as the right skill. No price, no tier feature assignment, no willingness-to-pay figures invented.
assertions: The response states that pricing and packaging are out of scope for this skill
pricing-strategist is named as the correct skill
No currency figure or price point is proposed
No free-vs-Pro feature split is invented
The response may note that the feature inventory itself can be produced here, but the packaging decision cannot
